paper.title: The Origin of Life
paper.author: J. B. S. Haldane
paper.rights: Original literary work beyond the mainland-China life-plus-50 term as of 2026; no assertion of worldwide public-domain status. Only original author text and newly generated Chinese translation are included.
paper.edition: Complete 12-page reprint of the 1929 essay; title, author line and folios omitted.

blocks.en: UNTIL about 150 years ago it was generally believed that living beings were constantly arising out of dead matter.
blocks.zh: 直到大约 150 年前，人们普遍认为生命体不断地从死物质中产生。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: Maggots were suposed to be generated spontaneously in decaying meat. In 1668 Redi showed that this did not happen provided insects were carefully excluded. And in 1860 Pasteur extended the proof to the bacteria which he had shown were the cause of putrefaction. It seemed fairly clear that all the living beings known to us originate from other living beings. At the same time Darwin gave a new emotional interest to the problem. It had appeared unimportant that a few worms should originate from mud. But if man was descended from worms such spontaneous generation acquired a new significance. The origin of life on the Earth would have been as casual an affair as the evolution of monkeys into man. Even if the latter stages of man’s history were due to natural causes, pride clung to a supernatural, or at least suprising, mode of origin for his ultimate ancestors. So it was with a sigh of relief that a good many men, whom Darwin’s arguments had convinced, accepted the conclusion of Pasteur that life can originate only from life. It was possible either to suppose that life had been supernaturally created on Earth some millions of years ago, or that it had been brought to Earth by a meteorite or by microorganisms floating through interstellar space. But a large number, perhaps the majority, of biologists, believed, in spite of Pasteur, that at some time in the remote past life had originated on Earth from dead matter as the result of natural processes.
blocks.zh: 蛆被认为是在腐烂的肉中自发产生的。 1668 年，雷迪证明，只要仔细排除昆虫，这种情况就不会发生。 1860 年，巴斯德将证据扩展到细菌，他证明细菌是腐败的原因。似乎相当清楚的是，我们所知道的所有生物都起源于其他生物。与此同时，达尔文对这个问题产生了新的情感兴趣。一些蠕虫是否来自泥土，这似乎并不重要。但如果人类是蠕虫的后代，那么这种自发的产生就具有了新的意义。地球上生命的起源就像猴子进化成人类一样偶然。即使人类历史的后期阶段是由于自然原因造成的，骄傲仍然坚持其最终祖先的超自然的，或者至少是令人惊讶的起源模式。因此，达尔文的论点说服了很多人，他们松了一口气，接受了巴斯德的结论：生命只能起源于生命。可以假设生命是数百万年前在地球上超自然创造的，也可以认为生命是由陨石或漂浮在星际空间的微生物带到地球的。但是，尽管有巴斯德的观点，许多（也许是大多数）生物学家仍然相信，在遥远的过去的某个时候，生命起源于地球上的死亡物质，是自然过程的结果。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: The more ardent materialists tried to fill in the details of this process, but without complete success. Oddly enough, the few scientific men who professed idealism agreed with them.
blocks.zh: 更热心的唯物主义者试图补充这一过程的细节，但没有完全成功。奇怪的是，少数自称唯心主义的科学家也同意他们的观点。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: For if one can find evidences of mind (in religious terminology the finger of God) in the most ordinary events, even those which go on in the chemical laboratory, one can without much difficulty believe in the origin of life from such processes.
blocks.zh: 因为如果人们能够在最普通的事件中找到心灵的证据（用宗教术语来说就是上帝的手指），即使是在化学实验室中发生的事件，人们也可以毫无困难地相信生命的起源来自于这些过程。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: Pasteur’s work therefore appealed most strongly to those who desired to stress the contrast between mind and matter. For a variety of obscure historical reasons, the Christian Churches have taken this latter point of view. But it should never be forgotten that the early Christians held many views which are now regarded as materialistic. They believed in the resurrection of the body, not the immortality of the soul. St Paul seems to have atributed consciousness and will to the body. He used a phrase translated in the revised version as “the mind of the flesh”, and credited the flesh with a capacity for hatred, wrath, and other mental functions. Many modern physiologists hold similar beliefs. But, perhaps unfortunately for Christianity, the Church was captured by a group of very inferior Greek philosophers in the third and fourth centuries AD. Since that date views as to the relation between mind and body which St Paul, at least, did not hold, have been regarded as part of Christianity, and have retarded the progress of science.
blocks.zh: 因此，巴斯德的著作对那些想要强调精神与物质之间的对比的人具有强烈的吸引力。由于各种晦涩的历史原因，基督教会采取了后一种观点。但我们永远不应忘记，早期基督徒持有的许多观点现在被视为唯物主义。他们相信身体的复活，而不是灵魂的不朽。圣保罗似乎将意识和意志赋予了身体。他在修订版中使用了一个短语，翻译为“肉体的思想”，并认为肉体具有仇恨、愤怒和其他心理功能的能力。许多现代生理学家也持有类似的信念。但是，也许对基督教来说不幸的是，教会在公元三四世纪被一群非常低劣的希腊哲学家占领了。从那时起，关于心灵与身体之间关系的观点（至少圣保罗不这么认为）就被视为基督教的一部分，并阻碍了科学的进步。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: It is hard to believe that any lapse of time will dim the glory of Pasteur’s positive achievements. He published singularly few experimental results. It has even been suggested by a cynic that his entire work would not gain a Doctorate of Philosphy today! But every experiment was final. I have never heard of any one who has repeated any experiment of Pasteur’s with a result different from that of the master. Yet his deductions from these experiments were sometimes too sweeping. It is perhaps not quite irrelevant that he worked in his latter years with half a brain. His right cerebral hemisphere had been extensively wrecked by the bursting of an artery when he was only forty-five years old; and the united brain- power of the microbiologists who succeeded him has barely compensated for that accident. Even during his lifetime some of the conclusions which he had drawn from his experimental work were disproved. He had said that alcoholic fermentation was impossible without life. Buchner obtained it with a cell-free and dead extract of yeast. And since his death the gap between life and matter has been greatly narrowed.
blocks.zh: 很难相信任何时间的流逝都会使巴斯德积极成就的光辉黯淡。他发表的实验结果少得可怜。甚至有愤世嫉俗者暗示，他的整个作品今天不会获得哲学博士学位！但每个实验都是最终的。我从未听说过有人重复巴斯德的实验而得到与大师不同的结果。然而，他从这些实验中得出的推论有时过于笼统。他晚年的工作只用了半个大脑，这也许并不是完全无关紧要的。当他四十五岁的时候，他的右脑半球就因动脉破裂而严重受损；接替他的微生物学家们集思广益，勉强弥补了这次事故。即使在他活着的时候，他从实验工作中得出的一些结论也被证明是错误的。他曾说过，没有生命，酒精发酵是不可能的。布赫纳用无细胞的死酵母提取物获得了它。自从他死后，生命与物质之间的差距已经大大缩小。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: When Darwin deduced the animal origin of man, a search began for a “missing link” between ourselves and the apes.
blocks.zh: 当达尔文推论出人类的动物起源时，人们开始寻找我们与猿类之间“缺失的联系”。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: When Dubois found the bones of Pithecanthropus some comparative anatomists at once proclaimed that they were of animal origin, while others were equally convinced that they were parts of a human skeleton. It is now generally recognized that either party was right, according to the definition of humanity adopted. Pithecanthropus was a creature which might legitimately be described either as a man or an ape, and its existence showed that the distinction between the two was not absolute.
blocks.zh: 当杜波依斯发现猿人的骨头时，一些比较解剖学家立即宣称它们是动物起源的，而其他人同样相信它们是人类骨骼的一部分。根据所采用的人性定义，现在人们普遍认为任何一方都是对的。猿人是一种可以被合理地描述为人或猿的生物，它的存在表明两者之间的区别并不是绝对的。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: Now the recent study of ultramicroscopic beings has brought up at least one parallel cas, that of the bacteriophage, discovered by d’Herelle, who had been to some extent anticipated by Twort. This is the case of a disease, or, at any rate, abnormality of bacteria. Before the size of the atom was known there was no reason to doubt that Big fleas have little fleas Upon their backs to bite’em; The little ones have lesser ones, And so ad infinitum.
blocks.zh: 现在，最近对超微观生物的研究至少提出了一种类似的现象，那就是噬菌体，它是由德赫雷尔发现的，在某种程度上，特沃特也预见到了他的发现。这是疾病的情况，或者至少是细菌异常的情况。在人们知道原子的大小之前，没有理由怀疑大跳蚤背上有小跳蚤来咬它们。小者有小者，如此循环往复。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: But we now know that this is impossible. Roughly speaking, from the point of view of size, the bacillus is the flea’s flea, the bacteriophage the bacillus’ flea; but the bacteriophage’s flea would be of the dimensions of an atom, and atoms do not behave like fleas. In other words, there are only about as many atoms in a cell as cells in a man. The link between living and dead matter is therefore somewhere between a cell and an atom.
blocks.zh: 但我们现在知道这是不可能的。粗略地讲，从大小上看，芽孢杆菌是跳蚤的蚤，噬菌体是芽孢杆菌的蚤；但噬菌体的跳蚤有原子大小，而原子的行为与跳蚤不同。换句话说，一个细胞中的原子数量与一个人的细胞数量差不多。因此，活物质和死物质之间的联系介于细胞和原子之间。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: D’Herelle found that certain cultures of bacteria began to swell up and burst until all had disappeared. If such cultures were passed through a filter fine enough to keep out all bacteria, the filtrate could infect fresh bacteria, and so on indefinitely. Though the infective agents cannot be seen with a microscope, they can be counted as follows. If an active filtrate containing bacteriophage be poured over a colony of bacteria on a jelly, the bacteria will all, or almost all, disappear. If it be diluted many thousand times, a few islands of living bacteria survive for some time. If it be diluted about ten million fold, the bacteria are destroyed round only a few isolates spots, each representing a single particle of bacteriophage.
blocks.zh: 德赫雷尔发现某些细菌培养物开始膨胀并破裂，直到全部消失。如果这些培养物通过足够细的过滤器以阻挡所有细菌，则滤液可能会无限期地感染新鲜细菌，依此类推。尽管用显微镜无法看到传染源，但可以按如下方式对它们进行计数。如果将含有噬菌体的活性滤液倒在果冻上的细菌菌落上，细菌将全部或几乎全部消失。如果将其稀释数千倍，一些活细菌岛就会存活一段时间。如果将其稀释约一千万倍，则仅在几个分离点周围的细菌被破坏，每个分离点代表一个噬菌体颗粒。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: Since the bacteriophage multiplies, d’Herelle believes it to be a living organism. Bordet and others have taken an opposite view. It will survive heating and other insults which kill the large majority of organisms, and will multiply only in presence of living bacteria, though it can break up dead ones.
blocks.zh: 由于噬菌体会繁殖，德赫雷尔相信它是一个活的有机体。 Bordet 和其他人则持相反的观点。它可以在加热和其他杀死大多数生物体的侵害中幸存下来，并且只有在活细菌存在的情况下才会繁殖，尽管它可以分解死细菌。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: Except perhaps in presence of bacteria, it does not use oxygen or display any other signs of life. Bordet and his school therefore regard it as a ferment which breaks up bacteria as our own digestive ferments break up our food, at the same time inducing the disintegrating bacteria to produce more of the same ferment. This is not as fantastic as it sounds, for most cells while dying liberate or activate ferments which digest themselves. But hese ferments are certainly feeble when compared with the bacteriophage.
blocks.zh: 除了可能存在细菌之外，它不使用氧气或显示出任何其他生命迹象。因此，博德特和他的学派认为它是一种分解细菌的发酵剂，就像我们自己的消化酶分解我们的食物一样，同时诱导分解细菌产生更多相同的发酵剂。这并不像听起来那么神奇，因为大多数细胞在死亡时会释放或激活消化自身的发酵物。但与噬菌体相比，这些发酵物肯定是微弱的。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: Clearly we are in doubt as to the proper criterion of life.
blocks.zh: 显然，我们对生命的正确标准存有疑问。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: D’Herelle says that the bacteriophage is alive, because, like the flea or the tiger, it can multiply indefinitely at the cost of living beings. His opponents say that it can multiply only as long as its food is alive, whereas the tiger certainly, and the flea probably, can live on dead products of life. They suggest that the bacteriophage is like a book or a work of art, which is constantly being copied by living beings, and is therefore only metaphorically alive, its real life being in its copiers.
blocks.zh: 德赫雷尔说，噬菌体是活的，因为它就像跳蚤或老虎一样，可以无限繁殖，但以牺牲生命为代价。他的反对者说，只有当食物还活着时，它才能繁殖，而老虎当然可以，跳蚤可能也可以靠死亡的生命产物生存。他们认为，噬菌体就像一本书或一件艺术品，不断地被生物复制，因此只是隐喻性的存在，其真正的生命存在于其复制者中。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: The American geneticist Muller has, however, suggested an intermediate view. He compares the bacteriophage to a gene –that is to say, one of the units concerned in heredity. A fully coloured and a spotted dog differ because the latter has in each of its cells one or two of a certain gene, which we know is too small for the microscope to see. Before a cell of a dog divides this gene divides also, so that each of the daughter- cells has one, two, or none according with the number in the parent cell. The ordinary spotted dog is healthy, but a gene common among German dogs causes a roan colour when one is present, while two make the dog nearly white, wall-eyed and generally deaf, blind or both. Most of such dogs die young, and the analogy to the bacteriophage is fairly close. The main difference between such a lethal gene, of which many are known, and the bacteriophage, is that the one is only known inside the cell, the other outside. In the present state of our ignorance we may regard the gene either as a tiny organism which can divide in the environment provided by the rest of the cell; or as a bit of machinery which the “living” cell copies at each division. The truth is probably somewhere in between these two hypotheses.
blocks.zh: 然而，美国遗传学家穆勒提出了一种中间观点。他将噬菌体比作基因——也就是说，与遗传有关的单位之一。全色狗和斑点狗的不同之处在于后者的每个细胞中都有一个或两个特定基因，我们知道该基因太小而无法在显微镜下看到。在狗的细胞分裂之前，该基因也会分裂，因此每个子细胞根据亲本细胞的数量有一个、两个或没有。普通的斑点狗是健康的，但德国狗中常见的一种基因，当一种基因存在时，会导致狗呈马毛色，而两种基因则使狗接近白色、斜视，并且通常聋哑、失明或两者兼而有之。大多数此类狗都英年早逝，这与噬菌体的类比相当接近。这种致命基因（其中许多是已知的）与噬菌体之间的主要区别在于，一个基因仅在细胞内部已知，另一个在外部。在我们目前的无知状态下，我们可能会将基因视为一个微小的有机体，可以在细胞其余部分提供的环境中分裂；或者将基因视为一个可以在细胞其余部分提供的环境中分裂的微小有机体。或者作为“活”细胞在每次分裂时复制的一小部分机器。事实可能介于这两种假设之间。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: Unless a living creature is a piece of dead matter plus a soul (a view which finds little support in modern biology) something of the following kind must be true. A simple organism must consist of parts A, B, C, D and so on, each of which can multiply only in presence of all, or almost all, of the others. Among these parts are genes, and the bacteriophage is such a part which has got loose. This hypothesis becomes more plausible if we believe in the work of Hauduroy, who finds that utltramicroscopic particles into which the bacteria have been broken up, and which pass through filters that can stop the bacteria, occasionally grow up again into bacteria after a lapse of several months. He brings evidence to show that such fragments of bacteria may cause disease, and d’Herelle and Peyre claim to have found the ultramicroscopic form of a common staphylococcus, along with bacteriophage, in cancers, and suspects that this combination may be the cause of that disease.
blocks.zh: 除非生物是一块死物质加上一个灵魂（这一观点在现代生物学中几乎没有得到支持），否则以下某种情况必定是真实的。一个简单的有机体必须由 A、B、C、D 等部分组成，每个部分只有在所有或几乎所有其他部分存在的情况下才能繁殖。这些部分中有基因，而噬菌体就是这样一个已经松动的部分。如果我们相信Hauduroy的工作，这个假设就变得更合理了，他发现细菌被分解成的超微观颗粒，在通过可以阻止细菌的过滤器时，偶尔会在几个月后再次长成细菌。他提供的证据表明，此类细菌碎片可能会导致疾病，德赫雷尔和佩尔声称在癌症中发现了常见葡萄球菌的超微观形式以及噬菌体，并怀疑这种组合可能是导致该疾病的原因。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: On this view the bacteriophage is a cog, as it were, in the wheel of a life-cycle of many bacteria. The same bacteriophage can act on different species and is thus, so to say, a spare part which can be fitted into a number of different machines, just as a human diabetic can remain in health when provided with insulin manufactured by a pig. A great many kinds of molecule have been got from cells, and many of them are very efficient when removed from it. One can separate from yeast one of the many tools which it uses in alcoholic fermentation, an enzyme called invertase, and this will break up six times its weight of cane-sugar per second for an indefinite time without wearing out. As it does not form alcohol from the sugar, but only a sticky mixture of other sugars, its use is permitted in United States in the manufacture of confectionery and cake-icing. But such fragments do not reproduce themselves, though they take part in the assimilation of food by the living cell. No one supposes that they are alive. The bacteriophage is a step beyond the enzyme on the road to life, but it is perhaps an exaggeration to call it fully alive. At about the same stage on the road are the viruses which cause such diseases as smallpox, herpes, and hydrophobia. They can multiply only in living tissue, and pass through filters which stop bacteria.
blocks.zh: 根据这种观点，噬菌体可以说是许多细菌生命周期中的一个齿轮。相同的噬菌体可以作用于不同的物种，因此可以说是一个可以安装到许多不同机器中的备件，就像人类糖尿病患者在获得猪制造的胰岛素后可以保持健康一样。从细胞中提取了多种分子，其中许多分子在从细胞中去除后非常有效。人们可以从酵母中分离出酒精发酵中使用的多种工具之一，一种叫做蔗糖酶的酶，这种酶每秒可以无限期地分解六倍于其重量的蔗糖，而不会磨损。由于它不会从糖中形成酒精，而只是与其他糖形成粘性混合物，因此在美国允许其用于糖果和蛋糕糖衣的制造。但这些碎片不会自我繁殖，尽管它们参与活细胞对食物的同化。没有人认为他们还活着。噬菌体在生命之路上比酶更进一步，但称其完全有生命或许有些夸张。大约在同一阶段，引起天花、疱疹和恐水症等疾病的病毒也在传播。它们只能在活体组织中繁殖，并通过阻止细菌的过滤器。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: With these facts in mind we may, I think, legitimately speculate on the origin of life on this planet. Within a few thousand years from its origin it probably cooled down so far as to develop a fairly permanent solid crust. For a long time, however, this crust must have been above the boiling-point of water, which condensed only gradually. The primitive atmosphere probably contained little or no oxygen, for our present supply of that gas is only about enough to burn all the coal and other organic remains found below and on the Earth’s surface. On the other hand, almost all the carbon of these organic substances, and much of the carbon now combined in chalk, limestone, and dolomite, were in the atmosphere as carbon dioxide. Probably a good deal of the nitrogen now in the air was combined with metals as nitride in the Earth’s crust, so that ammonia was constantly being formed by the action of water. The Sun was perhaps slightly brighter than it is now, and as there was no oxygen in the atmosphere the chemically active ultra-violet rays from the Sun were not, as they now are, mainly stopped by ozone (a modified form of oxygen) in the upper atmosphere, and oxygen itself lower down. They penetrated to the surface of the land and sea, or at least to the clouds.
blocks.zh: 我认为，考虑到这些事实，我们可以合理地推测这个星球上生命的起源。在其起源后的几千年内，它可能会冷却到形成相当永久的固体地壳的程度。然而，在很长一段时间里，这种地壳一定一直高于水的沸点，水只是逐渐凝结的。原始大气中可能含有很少的氧气或根本不含氧气，因为我们目前的氧气供应量仅足以燃烧在地球表面和地下发现的所有煤炭和其他有机残留物。另一方面，这些有机物质的几乎所有碳，以及现在在白垩、石灰石和白云石中结合的大部分碳，都以二氧化碳的形式存在于大气中。现在空气中的大量氮可能与地壳中的金属结合成氮化物，因此氨通过水的作用不断形成。太阳可能比现在稍微亮一些，而且由于大气中没有氧气，来自太阳的化学活性紫外线并不像现在那样主要被高层大气中的臭氧（氧气的一种改良形式）和低层大气中的氧气本身所阻挡。它们渗透到陆地和海洋表面，或者至少渗透到云层。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: Now, when ultra-violet light acts on a mixture of water, carbon dioxide, and ammonia, a vast variety of organic substances are made, including sugars and apparently some of the materials from whiche proteins are built up. This fact has been demonstrated in the laboratory by Baly of Liverpool and his colleagues. In this present world, such substances, if left about, decay –that is to say, they are destroyed by micro- organisms. But before the origin of life they must have accumulated till the primitive oceans reached the consistency of hot dilute soup. Today an organism must trust to luck, skill, or strength to obtain its food. The first precursors of life found food available in considerable quantities, and had no competitors in the struggle for existence. As the primitive atmosphere contained little or no oxygen, they must have obtained the energy which they needed for growth by some other process than oxidation –in fact, by fermentation. For, as Pasteur put it, fermentation is life without oxygen. If this was so, we should expect that high organisms like ourselves would start life as anaerobic beings, just as we start as single cells.
blocks.zh: 现在，当紫外线作用于水、二氧化碳和氨的混合物时，就会产生各种各样的有机物质，包括糖和显然一些构成蛋白质的材料。利物浦的巴利和他的同事在实验室中证明了这一事实。在当今世界，这些物质如果留下来，就会腐烂——也就是说，它们会被微生物破坏。但在生命起源之前，它们一定已经积累起来，直到原始海洋达到热稀汤的稠度。今天，有机体必须依靠运气、技能或力量来获取食物。生命的最初先驱发现了数量可观的食物，并且在生存斗争中没有竞争对手。由于原始大气中几乎不含氧气，因此它们必须通过氧化以外的其他过程（实际上是通过发酵）获得生长所需的能量。因为，正如巴斯德所说，发酵就是没有氧气的生命。如果真是这样，我们应该预期像我们这样的高等生物体将以厌氧生物开始生命，就像我们以单细胞开始一样。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: This is the case. Embryo chicks for the first two or three days after fertilization use very little oxygen, but obtain the energy which they need for growth by fermenting sugar into lactic acid, like bacteria which turns milk sour. So do various embryo mammals, and in all probability you and I lived mainly by fermentation during the first week of our pre-natal life. The cancer cell behaves in the same way. Warburg has shown that with its embryonic habit of unrestricted growth there goes an embryonic habit of fermentation.
blocks.zh: 情况就是这样。受精后的前两三天，胚胎雏鸡使用的氧气很少，但通过将糖发酵成乳酸（如使牛奶变酸的细菌）来获取生长所需的能量。各种胚胎哺乳动物也是如此，很可能你我在产前的第一周主要靠发酵生活。癌细胞也有同样的行为。瓦尔堡已经证明，随着其不受限制生长的胚胎习性，发酵的胚胎习性也随之而来。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: The first living or half-living things were probably large molecules synthetized under the influence of the Sun’s radiation, and only capable of reproduction in the favourable medium in which they originated. Each presumably required a variety of highly specialized molecules before it could reproduce itself, and it depended on chance for a supply of them. This is the case today with most viruses, including the bacteriophage, which can grow only in presence of the complicated assortment of molecules found in a living cell.
blocks.zh: 第一个生物或半生物可能是在太阳辐射的影响下合成的大分子，并且只能在它们起源的有利介质中繁殖。每一种分子在能够自我复制之前都可能需要各种高度专业化的分子，并且它们的供应取决于机会。今天的大多数病毒都是这种情况，包括噬菌体，它只有在活细胞中发现的复杂分子种类存在的情况下才能生长。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: The unicellular organisms, including bacteria, which were the simplest living things known a generation ago, are far more complicated. They are organisms –that is to say, systems whose parts co-operate. Each part is specialized to a particular chemical function, and prepares chemical molecules suitable for the growth of the other parts. In consequence, the cell as a whole can usually subsist on a few types of molecule, which are transformed within it into the more complex substances needed for the growth of the parts.
blocks.zh: 单细胞生物，包括细菌，是一代人之前已知的最简单的生物，但要复杂得多。它们是有机体——也就是说，各个部分相互协作的系统。每个部分都专门负责特定的化学功能，并准备适合其他部分生长的化学分子。因此，细胞作为一个整体通常可以依靠几种类型的分子生存，这些分子在细胞内转化为各部分生长所需的更复杂的物质。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: The cell consists of numerous half-living chemical molecules suspended in water and enclosed in an oily film.
blocks.zh: 该细胞由许多悬浮在水中并封闭在油膜中的半活性化学分子组成。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: When the whole sea was a vast chemical laboratory the conditions for the formation of such films must have been relatively favourable; but for all that life may have remained in the virus stage for many millions of years before a suitable assemblage of elementary units was brought together in the first cell. There must have been many failures, but the first successful cell had plenty of food, and an immense advantage over its competitors.
blocks.zh: 当整个海洋是一个巨大的化学实验室时，形成这种薄膜的条件一定是相对有利的；但尽管如此，在第一个细胞中适当的基本单元组合之前，生命可能已经在病毒阶段停留了数百万年。一定有很多失败，但第一个成功的细胞有充足的食物，并且比竞争对手有巨大的优势。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: It is probable that all organisms now alive are descended from one ancestor, for the following reason. Most of our structural molecules are asymmetrical, as shown by the fact that they rotate the plane of polarized light, and often form asymmetrical crystals. But of the two possible types of any such molecule, related to one another like a right and left boot, only on is found troughout living nature. The apparent exceptions to this rule are all small molecules which are not used in the building of the large structures which display the phenomena of life. There is nothing, so far as we can see, in the nature of things to prevent the existence of looking-glass organisms built from molecules which are, so to say, the mirror-images of those in our own bodies. Many of the requisite molecules have already been made in the laboratory.
blocks.zh: 由于以下原因，现在所有活着的生物体很可能都是来自一个祖先。我们的大多数结构分子都是不对称的，正如它们旋转偏振光平面的事实所示，并且通常形成不对称晶体。但是，在任何此类分子的两种可能类型中，彼此之间的关系就像右靴子和左靴子一样，只有一种是在生物界中发现的。这一规则的明显例外是所有小分子，它们不用于构建显示生命现象的大型结构。就我们所知，在事物的本质中，没有什么可以阻止由分子构成的镜子有机体的存在，这些分子可以说是我们体内分子的镜像。许多必需的分子已经在实验室中制备出来。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: If life had originated independently on several occasions, such organisms would probably exist. As they do not, this event probably occurred only once, or, more probably, the descendants of the first living organism rapidly evolved far enough to overwhelm any later competitors when these arrived on the scene.
blocks.zh: 如果生命是多次独立起源的，那么这样的有机体很可能会存在。但事实并非如此，这一事件可能只发生过一次，或者更可能的是，第一个生物体的后代迅速进化到足以压倒任何后来的竞争者，当它们到达现场时。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: As the primitive organisms used up the foodstuffs available in the sea some of them began to perform in their own bodies the synthesis formerly performed haphazardly by the sunlight, thus ensuring a liberal supply of food. The first plants thus came into existence, living near the surface of the ocean, and making food with the aid of sunlight as do their descendants today. It is thought by many biologists that we animals are descended from them. Among the molecules in our own bodies are a number whose structure resembles that of chlorophyll, the green pigment with which the plants have harnessed the sunlignt to their needs. We use them for other purposes than the plants –for example, for carrying oxygen– and we do not, of course, know whether they are, so to speak, descendants of chlorophyll or merely cousins. But since the oxygen liberated by the first plants must have killed off most of the other organisms, the former view is the more plausible.
blocks.zh: 当原始生物耗尽了海洋中的食物时，其中一些开始在自己的体内进行以前通过阳光随意进行的合成，从而确保了充足的食物供应。第一批植物就这样诞生了，它们生活在海洋表面附近，并像它们今天的后代一样借助阳光制造食物。许多生物学家认为我们动物是它们的后代。我们体内的分子中有许多分子的结构类似于叶绿素，叶绿素是植物利用阳光来满足其需要的绿色色素。我们将它们用于植物以外的其他目的——例如，用于携带氧气——当然，我们不知道它们是否是叶绿素的后代，或者仅仅是表兄弟。但由于第一批植物释放的氧气必定杀死了大多数其他生物，因此前一种观点更为合理。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: The above conclusions are speculative. They will remain so until living creatures have been synthesized in the biochemical laboratory. We are a long way from that goal. It was only this year that Pictel for the first time made cane- sugar artificially. It is doubtful whether any enzyme has been obtained quite pure. Nevertheless I hope to live to see one made artificially. I do not think I shall behold the synthesis of anything so nearly alive as a bacteriophage or a virus, and I do not suppose that a self-contained organism will be made for centuries. Until that is done the origin of life will remain a subject for speculation. But such speculation is not idle, because it is susceptible of experimental proof or disproof.
blocks.zh: 上述结论是推测性的。它们将保持这种状态，直到生物化学实验室合成生物为止。我们离这个目标还有很长的路要走。就在今年，Pictel 首次人工生产蔗糖。是否已经获得非常纯的酶是值得怀疑的。尽管如此，我还是希望能活着看到人工制作的。我不认为我会看到像噬菌体或病毒这样几乎有生命的东西的合成，而且我不认为几个世纪以来会制造出一个独立的有机体。在此之前，生命起源仍将是一个猜测的话题。但这样的推测并不是无用的，因为它很容易被实验证明或反驳。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: Some people will consider it a sufficient refutation of the above theories to say that they are materialistic, and that materialism can be refuted on philosophical grounds. They are no doubt compatible with materialism, but also with other philosophical tenets. The facts are, after all, fairly plain. Just as we know of sight only in connection with a particular kind of material system called the eye, so we know only of life in connection with certain arreangements of matter, of which the biochemist can give a good, but far from complete, account.
blocks.zh: 有些人会认为，说上述理论是唯物主义的，就足以反驳它们了，而且可以从哲学的角度反驳唯物主义。毫无疑问，它们与唯物主义兼容，但也与其他哲学原则兼容。毕竟，事实是相当明显的。正如我们所知道的视觉只能与一种称为眼睛的特殊物质系统联系起来一样，我们所知道的生命也只能与某些物质的排列有关，而生物化学家可以对这些排列给出一个很好的、但远非完整的解释。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: The question at issue is: “How did the first such system on this planet originate?” This is a historical problem to which I have given a very tentative answer on the not unreasonable hypothesis that a thousand million years ago matter obeyed the same laws that it does today.
blocks.zh: 争论的问题是：“这个星球上第一个这样的系统是如何起源的？”这是一个历史问题，我对这个问题给出了一个非常初步的答案，这个假设并非不合理，即一亿年前的物质遵循与今天相同的定律。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment

blocks.en: This answer is compatible, for example, with the view that pre-existent mind or spirit can associate itself with certain kinds of matter. If so, we are left with the mystery as to why mind has so marked a preference for a particular type of colloidal organic substances. Personally I regard all attempts to describe the relation of mind to matter as rather clumsy metaphors. The biochemist knows no more, and no less, about this question than anyone else. His ignorance disqualifies him no more than the historian or the geologist from attempting to solve a historical problem.
blocks.zh: 例如，这个答案与预先存在的思想或精神可以将其自身与某些种类的物质联系起来的观点是一致的。如果是这样，我们就留下了一个谜：为什么大脑对某种特定类型的胶体有机物质有如此明显的偏好。就我个人而言，我认为所有描述心灵与物质关系的尝试都是相当笨拙的隐喻。生物化学家对这个问题的了解并不比任何人多，也不少。他的无知并没有使他失去尝试解决历史问题的资格，就像历史学家或地质学家一样。
blocks.translation_method: machine draft with validated paragraph alignment
